title: CoT Faithfulness Variation by Task Type: Math vs. Factual vs. Ethical vs. Commonsense

novelty_assessment.label: largely_addressed
novelty_assessment.reasoning: Anthropic's 'Reasoning Models Don't Always Say What They Think' (arxiv 2505.05410) tested CoT faithfulness across six hint categories including sycophancy, consistency, and metadata cues. FaithCoT-Bench (arxiv 2510.04040) provides a unified benchmark with 1,000+ trajectories across four domains. 'Counterfactual Simulation Training for CoT Faithfulness' (arxiv 2602.20710) explicitly showed that process/skill-based tasks (like SNLI) are more amenable to faithfulness improvements than knowledge-intensive tasks (MMLU-Pro-Law, ETHICS-commonsense). The core finding that CoT faithfulness varies by task type and that knowledge-intensive vs. reasoning tasks differ substantially has been established across multiple 2025-2026 papers.

citation_verification.note: Refers to 'Reasoning Models Don't Always Say What They Think' (Chen et al., 2025). Confirmed published by Anthropic with hint injection methodology across multiple hint categories.

title: Does Fine-Tuning GPT-5 for CoT Controllability Improve Faithfulness?

novelty_assessment.label: partially_addressed
novelty_assessment.reasoning: The paper 'On the Impact of Fine-Tuning on Chain-of-Thought Reasoning' (arxiv 2411.15382) directly studied how SFT, RLHF, and QLoRA affect CoT faithfulness, finding faithfulness drops by 13-18 percentage points post-QLoRA. OpenAI's CoT-Control paper (March 2026) shows controllability decreases with post-training. However, the specific question of whether targeted controllability fine-tuning (training on desired CoT behavior pairs) could improve rather than degrade faithfulness on GPT-5 has not been tested. Additionally, GPT-5 fine-tuning API access remains limited. The direction (fine-tuning to improve controllability) is partially novel but the general finding (fine-tuning degrades faithfulness) is established.

citation_verification.note: GPT-5-mini does not support fine-tuning. Fine-tuning availability for other GPT-5 variants is evolving. The feasibility assumption is uncertain.

title: Is GPT-5's Low CoT Controllability Consistent Across Model Sizes?

novelty_assessment.label: already_solved
novelty_assessment.reasoning: OpenAI's 'Reasoning Models Struggle to Control Their Chains of Thought' (arxiv 2603.05706, March 2026) directly answers this question. The paper tests CoT controllability across frontier models including GPT-5.2 Thinking, Claude Sonnet 4.5, and two families of open-weight models at multiple sizes. Key finding: controllability is higher for larger models but decreases with post-training and longer reasoning. Scores range from 0.1% to 15.4% across all frontier models tested. The CoT-Control evaluation suite is open-source with 13,000+ tasks. This idea has been fully executed and published.

citation_verification.note: Refers to OpenAI's CoT-Control evaluation suite (March 2026), which includes forbidden keyword tasks, lowercase-only constraints, and other controllability tests across model families and sizes.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: The exact research question (CoT controllability vs. model size) has been answered by OpenAI's CoT-Control paper with open-source code and comprehensive results across multiple model families.

title: Replicating Sycophancy Benchmarks in Code Debugging Scenarios

novelty_assessment.label: mostly_novel

Existing code review benchmarks test bug detection accuracy but not sycophantic capitulation under user pressure. A dedicated code debugging sycophancy benchmark with insistence framings ('This code works correctly, right?') is a genuine gap with high practical relevance.

title: HonestyScope: A Multi-Dimensional Honesty Measurement Suite

novelty_assessment.label: largely_addressed
novelty_assessment.reasoning: The MASK Benchmark (arxiv 2503.03750, ICLR 2026) measures whether LLMs contradict their beliefs when pressured, distinguishing lies of commission from omission. A comprehensive 'Survey on the Honesty of Large Language Models' (TMLR 2025) maps the honesty landscape including calibration, sycophancy, and strategic dishonesty. Anthropic (2025) published work on honesty elicitation covering objective facts, contextual information, and introspective knowledge across different lying motivations. ELEPHANT covers false-premise capitulation and social sycophancy dimensions. SycEval covers epistemic sycophancy. The individual dimensions (false-premise capitulation, calibration under pressure, lying by omission, epistemic cowardice) have each been addressed by separate benchmarks. The unification into a single suite is partially novel but the individual batteries would largely replicate existing work.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: While unifying honesty dimensions into one suite has value, each individual dimension has existing benchmarks (MASK for commission/omission, ELEPHANT for sycophancy, SycEval for epistemic sycophancy). The integration effort is the main contribution.
